column3: Directly repeats immersion in heedlessness and the instruction to leave them there for a limited time.
Its reminder that provision comes from God only faintly frames the gifts later misread in this passage.
Shows that continuing deeds can lose all weight when their underlying rejection voids them.
Pairs hearts screened from the call with the defiant continuation of each side's deeds.
Develops the same passage's heedless posture as arrogant, hostile nighttime speech.
Its argument against powerless objects of worship does not clarify immersed hearts or their continuing deeds.
Names people as heedlessly absorbed in an exact parallel to the focus's gh am rah condition.
The supplied livestock and children only indirectly anticipate the passage's test of prosperity.
The challenge to alleged partners concerns creation and authority, not the focus's moral condition.
Identifies a diseased heart that deepens through lying and receives punishment, specifying inner corruption.
Shows the punitive outcry that follows within the same sequence, extending the focus's condition toward consequence.
Its protected return with favor does not illuminate heedlessness or the additional deeds described here.
Sealed hearts, hearing, and sight give a related account of why warning fails to penetrate.
Righteous action by the messengers supplies a nearby positive contrast to the deeds of the heedless.
The warning against turning back after a messenger's death concerns a different kind of reversal.
Its command for each side to act from its position frames the focus's continuing deeds as accountable commitments.
The restoration of power, wealth, and children in an earlier history adds no direct clarification.
Faith joined to righteous deeds supplies the positive alternative to purposeless continuing action.
Exclusive power to remove the coming event is not a reading of the heart's immersion or deeds.
The command not to cry for help names the immediate failure of rescue after the passage's warning develops.
The death-throes use of the same root gives a distinct, more literal form of overwhelming enclosure.
Its denial that any force can help apart from the Merciful does not clarify the focus.
The immediately preceding question exposes prosperity as misread, helping explain the heedless condition.
Voided works of fearful hypocrites provide only a secondary example of defective action.
Describes hearts, eyes, and ears left unused for understanding, a fuller profile of heedlessness.
Wealth and children as a trial sharpen the nearby warning against reading bestowed goods as approval.
Apparent freedom and success of disbelievers is a limited parallel to being deceived by present conditions.
Separates each party's deeds and responsibility, adding accountability to the focus's continuing actions.
The preceding unity and call to reverence frame the fragmentation and heedlessness that follow.
Associating partners renders deeds void, showing one decisive corruption of otherwise continuing action.
The fate of idols and their worshippers in Hell does not add to the specific inner condition.
The immediately preceding fearful hearts and return to the Lord form the focused moral counterpoint.
The magicians' defeat and humiliation do not clarify the focus beyond a remote reversal motif.
The blocked request to return and do righteousness contrasts present continued deeds with irreversible delay.
Solomon's military warning adds no meaningful connection to heedlessness or action.
The messenger's movement among worshippers does not clarify the focus's heart condition.
Commanded skillful work under divine sight supplies a concrete contrary model of responsible deeds.
The immediately prior record of truth and non-injustice establishes the accounting backdrop for their deeds.
Presumptuous confidence after mercy and later reporting of deeds offer a secondary analogue of misjudgment.
Distinguishes spoken belief from hearts that never believe, closely explaining an inner refusal beneath conduct.
The immediately preceding fragmentation into self-satisfied factions directly prepares the focus's adversative turn.
The sleepers' physical turning is unrelated to hearts immersed in heedlessness.
Questions whether diseased hearts, doubt, or fear drive refusal of judgment, specifying inward obstruction.
The division of Thamud after a call offers only a broad parallel to communal divergence.
Noah's refusal to judge followers' past deeds does not interpret the focus's additional deeds.
Worldly diversion and deception, followed by liability for what a soul earned, give a clear surrounding pattern.
The next verse identifies recited signs and turning back, explaining what the heedless hearts resist.
The heart as the locus of revelation is only a contrast to hearts closed to its force.
The failure of acquired gains and allies before Hell adds a distant consequence for worldly action.
The question about the Lord of the heavens and throne does not clarify the immediate moral diagnosis.
Faith made beloved and beautiful in hearts supplies a positive inner alternative to immersion.
The creation challenge to alleged partners does not address the focus's hearts or deeds.
Israel's refusal to enter the land gives a narrow example of disobedient action, without the focus's inner state.
Words that please while hearts refuse give a related split between outward conduct and inner disposition.
The Quran's account of Israelite disagreements does not materially clarify this condition.
The immediately preceding God-fearing group provides the opening counterprofile to those described in the focus.
God's knowledge of deeds in a testing context offers only general accountability for the focus's actions.
Names speech absent from hearts and affirms God's awareness of deeds, directly linking inward falsity and conduct.
God's non-negligence of creation is not a close reading of their immersed hearts.
The preservation of reward for excellent deeds is a broad positive contrast already supplied more concretely.
The doubled punishment for a specific public indecency does not clarify the focus.
Solomon's rejection of a gift lightly contrasts material delight with a truer evaluation of goods.
God's sight of all deeds provides general surveillance but adds little after the nearer accounting verses.
Gratitude joined to righteous work offers a concrete response opposite to heedless use of blessing.
The next item in the passage names belief in the Lord's signs, the direct alternative to heedless hearts.
Reward for workers is a general consequence of deeds without clarifying the corrupt inner condition.
The condemnation of fabricating a lie after clarification does not add to this reading.
Earlier rejection of a human messenger in the same surah supplies narrative background for later turning from signs.
A sound heart at return to God gives a compact inverse image of the focus's immersed heart.
The final reward for truthful people does not specifically clarify immersed hearts or their deeds.
The queen's proposed gift and awaited reply are unrelated to the focus's diagnosis.
The question about those most lost in deeds gives a direct category for failed action.
The challenge to alleged partners concerns creation and false assurances, not the focus's core relation.
The following rejection of association with the Lord further specifies the passage's positive counterpart.
Recompense for evil and excellent deeds clarifies that continuing deeds carry differentiated outcomes.
Its signs for discerning observers do not explain the focus's heedlessness.
The later prayerful believers supply an internal contrast to the heart condition and action of the focus group.
Earthly adornment as a test of best deeds lightly contextualizes deception by present goods.
Its general sign for believers adds no specific interpretation.
Fear cast into hostile hearts is a different emotional condition from heedless immersion.
Degrees and full repayment based on deeds specify how the focus's continuing actions are ultimately assessed.
The creation argument and widespread ignorance do not add to the focus's moral diagnosis.
The immediately prior statement says they do not perceive the true meaning of apparent good, directly leading into the focus.
Hearts given compassion but later failure to maintain a practice distinguish inward endowment from faithful continuation.
Repentance, gratitude, and righteous action give a broad positive path rather than clarifying the focus closely.
The tree's nourishment for eaters is unrelated to heedless hearts or deeds.
Abraham's sound heart provides another direct inverse to the focus's heart immersed in heedlessness.
Doubt and blindness regarding the Hereafter provide a close cognitive form of the focus's unawareness.
Professed belief followed by turning away describes conduct that exposes an uncommitted inner response.
Repentance accompanied by righteous work supplies a general corrective to defective deeds.
The command to continue acting until outcomes are known gives a distant accountability frame.
Return to God and disclosure of what people did establish a final reckoning for the focus's deeds.
The question for a healer at death does not illuminate the focus's condition.
Hearts nearly swerving under hardship describe a temporary strain, not the settled immersion here.
Entrance into gardens for believers who do righteous deeds is a broad positive outcome.
The rebuke of wanting false gods does not add to the focus beyond general wrongdoing.
Nightly seeking forgiveness is a remote devotional counterpoint to heedlessness.
Rejected excuses, observed deeds, and return to the Knower make conduct answerable despite claims.
Learning harmful magic despite knowledge offers a secondary case of knowingly pursuing damaging action.
The lesser punishment intended to prompt return provides a possible corrective to ongoing heedlessness.
Immediately completes the contrast: the vigilant believers hasten to good deeds, unlike the focus group's ongoing other deeds.
Directly joins what people kept earning to a covering that settles upon their hearts.
Pairs nearness of reckoning with people heedlessly turning away, closely matching the focus's absorbed inattention.
Describes turning from Lord's signs while forgetting what one's hands sent ahead, linking inward refusal and acquired deeds.
Hearts covered against understanding and ears made deaf provide a close mechanism for remaining unresponsive.
Coverings over hearts and heaviness in ears explain persistent aversion to the Quran's reminder.
Distinguishes physical sight from hearts that fail to understand, sharpening the focus on inward perception.
Following desire, then having heart and hearing sealed, gives a causal profile of heedless conduct.
Warns believers against hearts hardening over time away from God's remembrance, a temporal counterpath to immersion.
Satan's induced forgetfulness of God's remembrance closely characterizes the focus's absent awareness.
Hardened hearts and forgetting part of the reminder show how covenantal refusal persists inwardly.
Arrogance leads people to turn from signs and misread every path, extending the focus's resistance to guidance.
Turned hearts and sight after initial refusal describe a divinely exposed persistence in transgression and wandering.
Inner sickness increases with defilement until death, providing a progressive form of corrupt heart condition.
A sealed heart following outward profession of faith offers a concentrated inward explanation for failure to understand.
Hearts hardened against God's remembrance give a direct contrary condition to a breast opened to Islam.
The hardening of hearts beyond stones is a related but less specific image of moral unresponsiveness.
The sealing of hearts that do not know offers a general parallel already represented by more specific heart-sealing verses.
